english.html: main hidden and unpunished, at the point when the case was about to be judged, made the true Martin Guerre appear, as by a miracle,

notes.citation: A Latin sentence, source not identified: Oculus Dei acutus est, videt omnia. It is not a scriptural verse in this form; cf. Ecclesiasticus 23:19 (Vulgate 23:28), oculi Domini multo plus lucidiores sunt super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum, and Proverbs 15:3
notes.original: Oculus Dei acutus eſt, videt omnia.
notes.gloss: Possibly a schoolroom or emblem tag; Coras gives it as the ground of what follows.

english.html: Great certainly, and marvellous, is the goodness, grace and mercy of our God: which, when it pleases Him to pour it out upon us, there is no ruse, cunning or malignity of men, no inventions, wiles or malice of Satan, that can hinder it or offer it any resistance — as this deed here, after countless others, makes plain: two poor innocents, such as were Bertrande de Rols and Pierre Guerre, who by the strong hand of the Almighty were delivered from the imminent peril of death in which they (as calumniators) were placed; and the impudently measureless imposture of this wretched cheat du Tilh, as by a miracle, made manifest and discovered. And in truth it was indeed a miracle to make Martin Guerre appear — at whose expense all these pitiful games had been played — at the point when this case was about to be judged, in which the judges found themselves in incredible perplexity, and perhaps in danger of giving a judgment which would not altogether have answered to the justice of the cause, because the matters (in the opinion of many) were disposed more to the advantage of the prisoner, and against the said Pierre Guerre and de Rols: but the all-good and mighty God, who with His keen and piercing eye sees all things,
(The eye of God is keen; it sees all things — Oculus Dei acutus est, videt omnia)

and, being the sole searcher of men, sounds their deeds, contemplates and weighs their works <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, and who has left it written by the learned pen of His Prophets and Evangelists that there is nothing so covered, so secret, nor so hidden that in the end He does not reveal it and bring it to light <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup> — would not permit that so strange and impudently brazen a trickery, so scandalous an effrontery, so horrible and monstrous an imposture should remain concealed and unknown.

notes.citation: Acts 15 (15:8, "God, which knoweth the hearts"); 1 Thessalonians 2 (2:4, "God, which trieth our hearts")
notes.original: Actes c. xv la j des Theſſaloniſsiens. c. ij.
notes.gloss: God as the searcher of hearts.

notes.citation: Jeremiah 23 (23:24: can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him?); Ecclesiasticus 16 (16:17–21, Vulgate: the eye of God sees all) and 23 (23:19 Vulgate 23:28, as above); Matthew, Mark and Luke as printed (chapters v, iij and ij): the saying that nothing is hidden that shall not be revealed is at Matthew 10:26, Mark 4:22 and Luke 8:17 and 12:2; Coras's chapter numbers do not match the modern ones and are given as printed
notes.original: Ieremie c. xxiij. Eccleſiaſtique xvj. & xxiij. S. Matthieu v. S. Marc iij. S. Luc ij.
notes.gloss: The scriptural warrant that God brings every hidden thing to light.
